question: A moving coil galvanometer works on the torque experienced by a current loop in a magnetic field. Obtain the expression for torque on a current-carrying coil and hence derive the relation between current and deflection in a moving coil galvanometer. If $N=200$, $A=2.5\times10^{-4}\text{ m}^2$, $B=0.12\text{ T}$ and $k=5.0\times10^{-6}\text{ N m rad}^{-1}$, calculate the current required for a deflection of $0.40\text{ rad}$.

options.A: $\tau=NIAB\cos\theta$. In a radial magnetic field $\theta=90^\circ$, so $\tau=0$; hence no relation between current and deflection is obtained.
options.B: $\tau=NIAB\sin\theta$. In the radial field, $\theta=90^\circ$, so $\tau=NIAB$. At equilibrium, $NIAB=k\phi$, hence $I=\dfrac{k\phi}{NAB}$. Thus, $I=\dfrac{(5.0\times10^{-6})(0.40)}{(200)(2.5\times10^{-4})(0.12)}=3.33\times10^{-4}\,\text{A}$.
